evidence: The two reports share 66 NASA and USAF hypobaric chamber tests, 1,075 exposures, similar predictors and exclusion of paresthesia in the described DCS analysis. The 209 and 211 numerators differ for an unresolved reason. Treat the reports as overlapping.

NASA TP-2001-210775 references the 1996 model paper for the 66-test, 1,075-record fit. Its overall archive analysis has a broader scope. The 1996 paper separately reports the 52-group historical validation sample. Individual membership of the reports is unavailable.

The NASA report Figure 7 and the 1998 journal Figure 4 have the same ten bins, fitted cohort size of 1,322, and 168 DCS cases. Nine printed fractions match exactly. The first NASA label is 19/491, while the journal figure and text both report 19/941, which reconciles the aggregate and matches the plotted incidence. The bins are a subset analysis of the archival report, and do not contribute additional exposures to the 1998 journal cohort.
Page 181 describes 6/28 with exercise at 4.3 psia, six hours and TR360 1.60, matching NASA F1 3a. The group belongs to the derivation discussion.
Page 181 describes 7/17 without exercise at 4.3 psia for six hours. This is consistent with the published technician profile. No crosswalk of individuals is available.
